requirements.applies_when: Any person or business organization acting as a contractor in Florida for work in a regulated category.
requirements.fees: Varies by license type; see fee requirements
requirements.notes: Two licensure paths: CERTIFIED — pass the state competency examination, work anywhere in the state (certified license numbers begin with C). REGISTERED — hold a local (county/city) certificate of competency and register with the state; practice only in the jurisdiction(s) that issued the local competency card (numbers begin with R). A new business wanting statewide operation needs certified licensure; a business staying in one locality may use the registered path if the locality still issues local competency licenses. Per s. 489.117, registered contractors may also practice in adjoining locales that accept the registration.
requirements.timeline: Board must approve or deny an application within 90 days; licenses are typically issued within two weeks after the board meeting in which the application was approved.
requirements.title: Contractor licensing required before doing business — certified vs registered

requirements.applies_when: Contracting for any activity requiring licensure under Ch. 489 Part I, i.e., any type of construction work.
requirements.notes: Division I license (Div I = paragraphs (a)-(c)). Services are unlimited as to type of work; may contract for and perform any work requiring licensure under Part I, except as expressly provided in s. 489.113. Division I licenses (general/building/residential) carry higher financial-stability thresholds (up to $20,000 net worth/cash/bonding by rule, s. 489.115(7)).
requirements.title: License category: General Contractor (CGC)

requirements.applies_when: Building commercial buildings or residential buildings no more than three stories tall, or non-structural remodeling/repair of any size building.
requirements.notes: Division I. Limited to construction of commercial and single-/multiple-dwelling residential buildings not exceeding three stories in height, plus accessory-use structures; or remodeling/repair/improvement of any size building if services do not affect structural members.
requirements.title: License category: Building Contractor (CBC)

requirements.applies_when: Building, remodeling, repairing, or improving one-, two-, or three-family residences not exceeding the statutory height limit.
requirements.notes: Division I. Limited to one-family, two-family, or three-family residences not exceeding two habitable stories above no more than one uninhabitable story, plus accessory-use structures.
requirements.title: License category: Residential Contractor (CRC)

requirements.applies_when: Contracting in a specialty trade rather than general/building/residential construction.
requirements.notes: Division II categories per CILB FAQ: sheet metal; roofing; air-conditioning (Classes A/B/C); mechanical; swimming pool/spa (commercial, residential, servicing); plumbing; underground utility and excavation; solar; and pollutant storage. In addition, certified specialty contractor licenses (created by CILB rulemaking, e.g., specialty structure, gypsum drywall, marine, glass and glazing, tower, building demolition, irrigation, industrial facilities, rooftop solar heating, structural masonry, structural steel, etc., plus pool specialties) are voluntary statewide licenses obtainable instead of a local specialty license. Division II financial-stability thresholds cap lower (up to $10,000 by rule, s. 489.115(7)).
requirements.title: License categories: Division II trades and certified specialty contractors

requirements.applies_when: Seeking a certified contractor license by examination.
requirements.notes: Must be 18 years old and of good moral character, plus one of: (1) baccalaureate degree from an accredited 4-year college in engineering, architecture, or building construction plus 1 year of proven experience in the category; or (2) at least 4 years of active experience as a skilled worker/apprentice or foreman, with at least 1 year as a foreman. Minimum 2,000 person-hours = full-time equivalency. Trade-knowledge exam exemption available for applicants with a building-construction baccalaureate degree and 3.0+ GPA (then only the Business and Finance exam is required).
requirements.title: Eligibility to sit for the certification examination

requirements.applies_when: Seeking a certified contractor license by examination.

forms.name: Florida contractor's examination application (via Professional Testing, Inc. / Pearson VUE)

requirements.notes: Open-book exams. Trade Knowledge, Project Management, and Contract Administration given the same day; Business/Finance exam is 6.5 hours. Computer-based exams (except Plumbing Trade Knowledge) administered by Pearson VUE at sites statewide, available at any time. Only failed sections must be retaken (61G4-16.009). Active CILB licensees adding a category are exempt from the Business/Finance portion. NASCLA-accredited general/building/residential exams plus the Florida Business and Finance exam and a Florida Building Code exam can support endorsement (Form DBPR CILB 10). Alternative path: hold an out-of-state license for 10+ years and apply for endorsement (2-hour Florida Building Code / wind mitigation course required for Division I and roofing).
requirements.timeline: All exam portions must be completed within 4 years of the first attempt; after 4 years all scores expire and the full exam must be retaken. Application for licensure must be made within 4 years of passing.
requirements.title: State contractor examination — format, sections, retakes

forms.name: Application for initial certified contractor's license

requirements.notes: Four years of field experience in the category of licensure, including at least one year of supervisory experience. Up to 3 years of any military service (DD214) or any accredited college credit hours may substitute; at least one year of supervisory construction experience in the licensed category is still required. Special experience required for general/building: demonstrate experience in 4 of 6 categories (foundations/slabs over 20,000 sq ft, masonry walls, steel erection, elevated slabs, column erection, formwork for structural reinforced concrete); for general contractors, at least one year of such experience must be new construction of structures of at least 4 stories.
requirements.title: Experience documentation — 4 years field + 1 year supervisory

requirements.applies_when: Applying for initial certification or registration, requesting a change of status, or qualifying a business entity.
requirements.notes: Submit a credit report from a nationally recognized credit agency showing a FICO-derived credit score of 660 or higher, with a public-records statement that local, state, and federal records were checked. If the score is below 660, applicant must complete a board-approved 14-hour financial responsibility and stability course. Proof of satisfaction of liens, judgments, and discharge of bankruptcy required where applicable. For business qualification, credit reports are required on the qualifying agent AND both the presently qualified and proposed qualified businesses. A financially responsible officer (FRO) model exists: if the qualifier lacks financial responsibility, the business must appoint an FRO, who must hold a $100,000 surety bond or irrevocable letter of credit payable to the CILB (letter of bondability not accepted). Statutory net-worth/cash/bonding guidelines are capped at $20,000 for Division I and $10,000 for Division II certificateholders.
requirements.title: Financial responsibility — credit report and FICO 660 / 14-hour course or bond

requirements.applies_when: Initial issuance and renewal of any certificate or registration; active licensees must maintain coverage at all times.
requirements.notes: Submit board-form affidavit attesting to workers' compensation coverage per Ch. 440, public liability, and property damage insurance in board-determined amounts. CILB-published minimums: general and building contractors $300,000 liability / $50,000 property damage; all other categories $100,000 liability / $25,000 property damage (or amounts set by board rule). Active licensees must maintain workers' comp coverage OR an exemption; applicants may state they will obtain the exemption within 30 days of licensure.
requirements.timeline: Affidavit of insurance required before issuance and at each renewal; workers' compensation exemption (if applicable) must be obtained within 30 days of becoming licensed.
requirements.title: Insurance — general liability, property damage, workers' compensation affidavit

requirements.applies_when: Applying for initial licensure or qualifying a construction business.
requirements.notes: Electronic fingerprints and criminal-history disclosure are required (application checklists list electronic fingerprints and supporting legal documentation). The board may not deny licensure based solely on a felony conviction or failure to provide proof of restoration of civil rights (s. 489.115(6)), but criminal history, good moral character, and financial stability are review factors; applicants with concerns may be placed on probationary status and required to appear before the board twice annually. Number, severity, recency of convictions and rehabilitation efforts are weighed individually.
requirements.title: Fingerprint-based background check and criminal history disclosure

requirements.applies_when: Operating as a corporation, partnership, LLC, or any business entity other than a sole proprietorship; or operating as an individual under a business name.
requirements.fees: Statutory cap: $50 initial application fee and $50 renewal fee to qualify a business organization

forms.name: Application for initial licensure qualifying a business (e.g., DBPR CILB 6-series by category)

requirements.notes: Contractors must qualify their construction business with their individual license; the license is issued in the qualifying agent's name with the business name noted on it. The qualifying agent must have supervisory authority and final approval over all construction affairs. Qualifying an additional business requires a separate application (e.g., DBPR CILB 7-H for an additional business) and triggers board appearance if the applicant owns under 20% or would qualify 3+ businesses. If a qualifying agent resigns/is fired, the company has 60 days to obtain another qualifier (temporary nonrenewable license available); if the qualifier dies, notify the board within 30 days. Certificates of Authority (qualified business licenses) have not been issued since October 1, 2009.
requirements.title: Qualifying agent — business must be qualified by a licensed contractor

requirements.applies_when: Submitting any application for initial certification or registration.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. ss. 489.109(1)(a)-(c); DBPR CILB application instructions
requirements.fees: Initial certification: $245 if applying May 1 of an EVEN year through Aug 31 of an ODD year; $145 if applying Sept 1 of an ODD year through Apr 30 of an EVEN year. Statutory caps: certificate application fee ≤$150 (≤$350 combined with exam cost); certification and renewal fees ≤$250; registration application fee ≤$100; registration and renewal fees ≤$200.
requirements.notes: Mail completed application, documentation, and fees to DBPR, 2601 Blair Stone Road, Tallahassee, FL 32399-0783. Applications are also available through DBPR Online Services. Note registered-contractor application fee windows differ (odd/even year cycle); published registration fee examples ($205/$105) were seen in a third-party mirror of the state form — confirm current fee windows on the official form before paying.
requirements.timeline: Board must approve or deny within 90 days of application; applications are typically sent to the first board meeting after receipt (board does not meet in December).
requirements.title: Application fees and where to file

requirements.applies_when: Every CILB license holder at each biennial renewal.
requirements.fees: Delinquent fee $250; inactive-status fee $50 (no fee to become inactive during a renewal period). Statutory caps: renewal ≤$250 (certified) / ≤$200 (registered); inactive renewal ≤$50.
requirements.notes: Renew by completing, signing, and forwarding the renewal application with fee; delinquency fees may not exceed the renewal fee. Licensees whose licenses were not renewed by expiration are expired (may not practice) — reactivation requires the reactivation application, fee, and CE for the preceding cycle. A null-and-void license (not renewed for an extended period) generally requires starting over, including retaking the exam; reinstatement applications (Form DBPR CILB 26, $100 fee) exist for illness/economic hardship cases at DBPR discretion. Additional $4 per application/renewal funds building-construction industry research/CE per s. 489.109(3).
requirements.timeline: Certified contractors renew August 31 of every EVEN-numbered year; registered contractors renew August 31 of every ODD-numbered year. Inactive licenses must still be renewed every two years.
requirements.title: Renewal cycle and renewal/delinquent/inactive fees

requirements.applies_when: All active certified and registered contractors at each biennial renewal.
requirements.notes: 14 hours required, including at least 1 hour each in: Workplace Safety, Workers' Compensation, Business Practices, Advanced Module Building Code, and Laws and Rules. General, building, residential, roofing, specialty structure, and glass-and-glazing specialty contractors must also complete 1 hour of Wind Mitigation Methodology within the 14 hours; remainder are general credits. Reduced obligation for licenses issued mid-cycle: <12 months before renewal = no CE; 12-24 months = 7 hours general credits. Online courses available through providers designated C/I or I on the board's CE page. Core-course requirement was removed by the Legislature in 2009.
requirements.timeline: 14 hours due each 2-year renewal cycle (Aug 31 even years certified / odd years registered).
requirements.title: Continuing education — 14 hours per renewal cycle

requirements.applies_when: Any advertising, bidding, contracting, or permit application by a contractor or business.
requirements.citation: Fla. Stat. s. 489.119(5); Fla. Stat. s. 489.127
requirements.notes: Every registered or certified contractor must display the license number on any building-permit application; offer of service; business proposal; bid; contract; advertisement (including websites); sign; and vehicles displaying the contractor/business name. Engaging in contracting without the required certificate or registration is prohibited and subject to cease-and-desist, noncriminal fines (up to $500; $250/day for continuing violations), and criminal penalties under s. 489.127. Work not requiring a state license: cabinets, countertops, paint, wallpaper, carpet, tile, window treatments; handyman jobs under $2,500 total construction cost that are casual/minor/inconsequential are exempt from state licensure (local rules may still apply).
requirements.title: Advertising and permit rules — license number display; no contracting without license
